2025_095_m071525bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education meeting held July 15, 2025 at the Troy School District Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, called to order by President Philippart at 9:35 a.m. and adjourned at 10:18 a.m. The board approved consent agenda items A through G and then took three personnel actions: extending administrator contracts through June 30, 2026, extending the four assistant superintendents through June 30, 2027, and extending Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky's contract to run July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2030. Each vote was recorded as 6 yes, 0 no, with Zendler noted as absent/remote. The board released an evaluation describing Dr. Machesky as an exemplary superintendent.
2025_095_m071525bdmtg.page:
Meeting
Board of Education, Troy, Michigan. Regular board meeting, July 15, 2025, held at the Troy School District Administration Building, 4400 Livernois. Called to order by President Philippart at 9:35 a.m.; adjourned at 10:18 a.m. Minutes submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (notation EA/jh).

Attendance
Present: Dr. Philippart plus Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton and Potts. Mrs. Zendler attended via remote communications. Also present: Superintendent Machesky; administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Montante, Trudel and Pagel; and two members of the audience. Recognition, additions and deletions, and public communication were all recorded as none.

Consent Agenda
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Anne, to approve items A through G: minutes of the June 3, 2025 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the June 3, 2025 Closed Session Meeting; minutes of the June 3, 2025 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the June 17, 2025 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report for May 2025; settlement terms of Batista v Office of Retirement Services litigation; and rescheduling of the October 21st Board of Education Meeting and the December 2nd and January 6th Board Workshops. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent/Remote Zendler.

Personnel — Administrator Contract Extensions
Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Mrs. Alic, to extend the contracts of the listed administrators through June 30, 2026, or as otherwise indicated in the administrator's individual contract, without tenure in the administrative positions and subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook where applicable and as permitted by law. The list covered high school principals (Vernon Burden, Patrick Griffin, Remo Roncone), middle school principals (Ryan Brinks, Jonathan Cross, Anthony Morse, Brian Zawislak), eleven elementary principals, nine assistant principals, and five directors/supervisors. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent/Remote Zendler.

Assistant Superintendent Contracts
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic, to extend the contracts of Dan Trudel (Business Services), John Pagel (Employee Services), Kris Griffor (Elementary Instruction) and Christine DiPilato (Secondary Instruction) through June 30, 2027, without tenure in the administrative positions. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent/Remote Zendler.

Superintendent Evaluation and Contract
The board reported completing Dr. Richard Machesky's performance evaluation and shared an assessment rating him EXEMPLARY, having met or exceeded expectations in all evaluation categories. Points cited: continued execution of the strategic plan under the LEARNING FOR ALL vision; fiscal strength with sufficient fund balance to mitigate disruptions in state funding; a new business operations team integrated this year; bond projects tracking at or below budget; alignment and implementation of Multi-Tiered System of Support; new secondary assessments; math and literacy professional development; belonging, well-being and security initiatives; and all staff labor agreements negotiated and signed. The board committed to a more robust community-input process in curriculum evaluation and praised the Career Accelerator Program, run with the Business Roundtable, which provided 75 high school students with internships in local businesses. The minutes note that Dr. Machesky's contract then ran through June 30, 2029 and that the board planned to extend it by an additional year. Moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mrs. Anne, the extension was approved to be in effect July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2030, without tenure and subject to the provisions of the written Agreement. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent/Remote Zendler.

Other
Curriculum and Business items: none. Public communication on non-agenda items: none. Other items noted: summer work progress update, Data Dashboard update, and the MASB Conference in October. Dr. Philippart announced the next Board of Education meeting for August 19th at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building.
2025_095_m071525bdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of the Troy Board of Education meeting of July 15, 2025, held at the Troy School District Administration Building located at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan.

CALL TO ORDER AND ATTENDANCE
President Philippart called the meeting to order at 9:35 a.m. In addition to Dr. Philippart, Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton and Potts were present. Mrs. Zendler attended via remote communications. Also present were Superintendent Machesky; administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Montante, Trudel and Pagel; and two members of the audience. Recognition: none. Additions and deletions: none. Public communication: none.

CONSENT AGENDA
It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Anne that the Troy Board of Education take action to approve items A through G on the consent agenda: minutes of the June 3, 2025 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the June 3, 2025 Closed Session Meeting; minutes of the June 3, 2025 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the June 17, 2025 Board of Education Meeting; the Treasurer's Report for May 2025; the settlement terms of Batista v Office of Retirement Services litigation; and rescheduling of the October 21st Board of Education Meeting together with the December 2nd and January 6th Board Workshops. The vote was recorded as Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent/Remote: Zendler.

PERSONNEL — EXTENSION OF ADMINISTRATIVE PERSONNEL CONTRACTS
It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Alic that the Troy Board of Education approve the extension of the contracts of the named administrators through June 30, 2026, or as otherwise indicated in the administrator's individual contract, without tenure in the administrative positions and subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook, where applicable and as permitted by law.

High school principals: Vernon Burden, Principal, Athens High School; Patrick Griffin, Principal, International Academy-East; Remo Roncone, Principal, Troy High School.

Middle school principals: Ryan Brinks, Principal, Smith Middle School; Jonathan Cross, Principal, Baker Middle School; Anthony Morse, Principal, Boulan Park Middle School; Brian Zawislak, Principal, Larson Middle School.

Elementary principals: Michelle Barsh, Principal, Martell Elementary School; Karen Bush, Principal, Barnard Elementary School; Mike Cottone, Principal, Troy Union Elementary School; Erin Detmer, Principal, Leonard Elementary School; Tammy DiPonio, Principal, Costello Elementary School; Scott Keen, Principal, Morse Elementary School; Lindsay Keegan, Principal, Schroeder Elementary School; Shari Pawlus, Principal, Hill Elementary School; David Recker, Principal, Hamilton Elementary School; Harleen Singh, Principal, Bemis Elementary School; Amy Wallace, Principal, Wattles Elementary School.

Assistant principals: Kerry Brennan, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Melissa Curth, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Dan House, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Megan Henry, Assistant Principal, Athens High School; Gabrielle Naus, Assistant Principal, International Academy-East; Ross Burdette, Assistant Principal, Baker Middle School; Cassandra Conaton, Assistant Principal, Smith Middle School; Stephan Henning, Assistant Principal, Larson Middle School; Kristy Pierce, Assistant Principal, Boulan Park Middle School.

Directors and supervisors: Rob Carson, Director, Maintenance and Operations; Christine Foren, Supervisor, Special Education; Natalie Haezebrouck, Director, Teaching & Learning; Erin Keyser, Director, Early Childhood Program; Troy Wissink, Director, Technology.

The vote was recorded as Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent/Remote: Zendler.

EXTENSION OF ASSISTANT SUPERINTENDENT CONTRACTS
It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic that the Troy Board of Education approve the extension of the contracts for Dan Trudel, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services; John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services; Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction; and Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction, through June 30, 2027, without tenure in the administrative positions. The vote was recorded as Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent/Remote: Zendler.

SUPERINTENDENT EVALUATION
The minutes record that the Board recently completed Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky's performance evaluation and shared the resulting assessment with the community. The assessment states that Dr. Machesky is an EXEMPLARY superintendent who has met or exceeded expectations in all evaluation categories. It credits him with continuing to execute the district's strategic plan and driving high expectations for the vision of LEARNING FOR ALL as the basis for instructional decisions. It states the district remains fiscally strong under his leadership with sufficient fund balance to mitigate disruptions in state funding, that a new business operations team was integrated into the organization during the year, and that bond projects are tracking at or below budget. The district continues to focus on alignment and implementation of Multi-Tiered System of Support to address achievement gaps, particularly for special education students, English Language Learners and economically disadvantaged students. New assessments were put in place for secondary students to identify achievement gaps, and high-quality teacher professional development in math and literacy was provided for all grade levels. Several initiatives were put in place to increase students' sense of belonging, well-being and security. All staff labor agreements were successfully negotiated and signed during the year, providing the district with attractive compensation to retain and recruit staff. Going forward, Dr. Machesky and the board committed to developing a more robust process that gathers input and engages the community earlier in the curriculum evaluation process while still relying on the expertise of the district's educators for decision-making. The board also applauded Rich and the Business Roundtable for implementation of a growing, successful Career Accelerator Program that provided 75 high school students with internship opportunities in local businesses. The board expressed full confidence that he and his team have the capacity and capability to face future challenges.

EXTENSION OF SUPERINTENDENT CONTRACT
The minutes note that Dr. Machesky's contract at that time ran through June 30, 2029 and that the board planned to extend it by an additional year. It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne that the Troy Board of Education extend the contract of the Superintendent of Schools as described, with the contract to be in effect from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2030, without tenure in the administrative position and subject to provisions of the written Agreement. The vote was recorded as Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent/Remote: Zendler.

CURRICULUM, BUSINESS AND PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
No curriculum or business action items were recorded; the entries for these sections and for public communication on non-agenda items are marked none.

OTHER AND BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS
Items noted under other business and board member comments: a summer work progress update, a Data Dashboard update, and the MASB Conference in October.

ADJOURNMENT
Dr. Philippart shared that the next Board of Education Meeting would be held on August 19th at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building. The meeting was adjourned at 10:18 a.m. Respectfully submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education; typist notation EA/jh.
